memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the
LORD your God is giving you.'" - Ex 20:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This command sits at a hinge. The first four concern our relationship with God;
the last six concern people. And the first of those begins at home.

Notice the word: honour. Not "agree with," not "obey forever." Honour is
recognising the weight and worth of a person. Young children honour parents
largely by obeying. Adults honour them differently, through respect, care, and
provision as parents age.

Paul quotes this command and adds that it is "the first commandment with a
promise" (Eph 6:2). He also, in the same passage, tells fathers not to exasperate
their children, so the flow is not all one way.

Now, honesty is needed here. Some readers had parents who were cruel, absent, or
dangerous. Honour does not mean pretending abuse did not happen, and it does not
require placing yourself back within reach of harm. Jesus honoured His mother
from the cross by entrusting her to John's care (John 19:26-27), and He also
said that following Him sometimes divides families (Matt 10:35-36).

Honour may sometimes look like distance held without bitterness, and truth spoken
without revenge.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does honouring your parents look at this stage of your life?
2. Is there resentment you are carrying that needs bringing to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, help me to honour my parents rightly, with truth and without bitterness.
Where there is pain, bring healing. Amen.
